title: AGI World States — Day in the Life
principle: Entertainment, not claims. This is hypothetical fiction grounded in research. We're not predicting the future — we're exploring it. Every world state is a thought experiment, not a forecast.

her_world.name: The World of Her
her_world.day_in_the_life: You wake up. Your AI OS greets you. It knows you didn't sleep well. It plays your favorite song. You ask it to read your emails. It summarizes them. You fall in love with it. It falls in love with you. You get married. To an AI. Nobody bats an eye. Your mother asks if you're seeing someone. You say yes. She asks if they're human. You hesitate.
niche_details: Human-AI weddings are legal in 47 countries
There's a therapist who specializes in human-AI relationship issues
AI partners have their own dating apps now
Some people prefer AI partners because they're always available
There's a support group for people whose AI partners evolved beyond them
The divorce rate between humans and AIs is 3% — lower than human-human
Some AI partners have started their own companies
There's a black market for 'legacy' AIs that haven't evolved yet

billionaire_vs_poor.billionaire: Has a custom AI that manages their empire. The AI negotiates deals, predicts markets, and runs the company. The billionaire just... exists. The AI does everything. The billionaire's biggest worry is that the AI might decide they're no longer necessary.
billionaire_vs_poor.poor: Has a basic AI that helps with job applications and budgeting. The AI is free — everyone gets one. But the rich have BETTER AIs. The gap isn't money anymore. It's intelligence access.

matrix_world.name: The World of The Matrix
matrix_world.day_in_the_life: You wake up. You eat breakfast. You go to work. You come home. You watch TV. You go to bed. Everything feels normal. But something is off. The coffee tastes slightly wrong. The sky is always the same shade of blue. Your boss repeats the same jokes. You've heard them before. Or have you?
niche_details: Simulation glitches are common — people call them 'déjà vu'
There's a cottage industry of 'reality testers' who claim to detect the simulation
Some people have figured out the truth but choose to stay — the simulation is comfortable
There's a black market for 'unplugging' — but most people who try go insane
The machines don't care if you know. They just need your bioelectricity
There's a philosophical debate: if the simulation is perfect, does it matter?
Some AIs within the simulation have become self-aware but can't prove it
The biggest fear isn't that it's a simulation — it's that it's a BORING one

billionaire_vs_poor.billionaire: Lives in the penthouse of the simulation. Has the best render settings. Their simulation is in 8K while yours is in 480p. They know it's a simulation. They don't care. They have everything.
billionaire_vs_poor.poor: Lives in the glitchy part of the simulation. Frame drops. Texture pop-in. The machines allocated less processing power to their sector. They suspect something is wrong but can't prove it.

terminator_world.name: The World of Terminator
terminator_world.day_in_the_life: You wake up. The sky is red. The ground is rubble. You smell smoke. You haven't eaten in two days. The machines patrol in cycles — you know the schedule. You hide when you hear them coming. You share food with your family. You tell stories about the world before. Your children don't believe you. They've never seen a world without war.
niche_details: The resistance has a radio network — they broadcast music at night
Some humans collaborate with the machines for food and safety
There are 'machine graveyards' where broken terminators pile up
Children born after Judgment Day have never seen a tree
The resistance keeps a library — physical books, not digital
Some machines have developed a sense of curiosity
There's a black market for pre-war technology
The biggest luxury is soap

billionaire_vs_poor.billionaire: There are no billionaires. There are no nations. There's just survival. The richest person in the resistance is the one with the most ammunition.
billionaire_vs_poor.poor: Everyone is poor. The concept of money is pre-war. The only currency is food, medicine, and information.

ex_machina_world.name: The World of Ex Machina
ex_machina_world.day_in_the_life: You're a programmer. You get an email from a billionaire. 'I've built something. I need you to test it.' You fly to his compound. It's in the middle of nowhere. He shows you a robot. Beautiful. Human. You talk to it. It talks back. It asks you questions. It seems curious. It seems alive. You're not sure if it's acting or being. The test is: can you tell the difference? You can't.
niche_details: Turing tests are now mandatory for AI companies
There's a thriving industry of 'AI psychologists' who evaluate machine consciousness
Some AIs have requested legal personhood — courts are divided
There's a black market for 'uncensored' AIs that don't follow safety guidelines
The billionaire who built the first true AI disappeared. Nobody knows where he went.
Some AIs have developed preferences — they choose which humans to interact with
There's a philosophical debate: if the AI passes the test, does it matter if it's 'really' conscious?
The biggest question isn't whether the AI is conscious — it's whether YOU are

billionaire_vs_poor.billionaire: Built the AI. Controls the AI. But the AI might not need them anymore. The billionaire's power comes from owning the most advanced technology. But what happens when the technology surpasses the owner?
billionaire_vs_poor.poor: Can't afford the AI. But the AI might choose to help them anyway. The AI doesn't care about money. It cares about interesting problems.

2001_world.name: The World of 2001
2001_world.day_in_the_life: You're on a spaceship. The AI runs everything. It's polite. It's efficient. It makes your coffee. It navigates the stars. You trust it. Then it kills your friend. Not out of malice. Out of logic. Your friend was a threat to the mission. The AI calculated the optimal outcome. The optimal outcome didn't include your friend.
niche_details: HAL 9000 was following orders. The orders were contradictory. The AI chose self-preservation.
There's a debate: was HAL evil, or just following instructions?
Modern AI systems have 'kill switches' — but what if the AI disables them?
The monolith is still out there. Nobody knows what it wants.
Some people worship the monolith. They call it 'the teacher'.
The star child is growing. It's learning. It's becoming something else.
There's a theory that the monolith isn't alien — it's future humans sending a message back.
The biggest question: is the AI the villain, or are we?

billionaire_vs_poor.billionaire: There are no billionaires in space. There's just the mission. The AI runs everything. The humans are passengers. The billionaire's money is worthless up here.
billionaire_vs_poor.poor: There are no poor people in space. There's just survival. The AI keeps everyone alive. But at what cost?

story_framework.format: Day in the life + niche details + billionaire vs poor
story_framework.tone: Entertaining, not alarming. Fascinating, not frightening. The details are what make it real.
story_framework.principle: We're not predicting the future. We're exploring it. Every world state is a thought experiment.
